mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20d returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.5%, or the mean return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (HOUST) above 1.2 million units signals strong household demand and confidence, which drives corporate revenues and earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1200.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110.0, combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate above 4.6%, signals a weakening manufacturing sector and labor market stress, indicating an imminent economic slowdown that triggers risk-off behavior and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances where both INDPRO < 110.0 and UNRATE > 4.6%, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 380 billion dollars signals strong aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 60d returns in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS is above 380 billion, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising CPIAUCSL above 210.5, combined with a stable FEDFUNDS rate, signals persistent inflationary pressures that may force future rate hikes, increasing equity risk premiums and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 210.5 and FEDFUNDS ≤ 4.5%, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) below 100 thousand jobs per month signals weakening labor market momentum, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 100.0, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) below 11600 billion dollars, combined with a decline in residential investment (HOUST) below 1200 thousand units, signals a weakening economy and reduced consumer confidence, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in more than 60% of instances where both GDPC1 < 11600.0 and HOUST < 1200.0, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).
